# A Fast and Effective Solution to the Problem of Look-ahead Bias in LLMs

arXiv [2512.06607](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.06607) · v1 2025-12-07 · latest 2026-09-23

> **Machine-extracted method card.** The gloss column was written by `claude-opus-5-5` (effort medium) on 2026-10-23 from the html text of the paper. Every quote was checked by a program to be a passage of that text; the gloss has not been checked by a person. "Not found" means the model did not find the item in the text it was given, not that the paper omits it.

| Field | Gloss | Quote from the paper |
|---|---|---|
| **task** | Removing look-ahead bias from LLMs used for financial prediction/backtests by unlearning knowledge at inference time instead of retraining with a knowledge cutoff. | “In this paper, we introduce a fast, effective, and low-cost alternative. Our method guides generation at inference time by adjusting the logits of a large base model using a pair of smaller, specialized models—one fine-tuned on information to be forgotten and another on information to be retained.” |
| **architecture** | Divergence Decoding: a large frozen base model's logits are adjusted by the difference between two small models (forget-tuned p and retain-tuned q), either linearly with weight alpha or by blocking top-k most divergent tokens. | “Divergence Decoding (DD) approximates sampling from Q by adjusting the logits of P according to the divergence between q and p . Empirically, we consider two adjustments.” |
| **data** | MUSE news unlearning benchmark; 294 high-profile US public M&A deals from WRDS SDC (2010-01-01 to 2024-08-01), filtered to 41; airline (Southwest, United) performance reports for 2014-2016 and 2022-2024 generated by Gemma. | “We sample deals from Wharton Research Data Services, SDC - Mergers and Acquisitions, across the whole database, from 2010-01-01 to 2024-08-01, using the following filters to get 294 high profile conventional M&A deals.” |
| **window** | No backtest window; M&A deals span 2010-01-01 to 2024-08-01, split into two alternating chronological sets of 41 deals rotated as forget/retain; a per-deal prompt validation set used only for tuning. | “split the remaining 41 deals into two sets by selecting alternating deals chronologically.” |
| **models** | Small models: princeton-nlp/Sheared-LLaMA-1.3B, Sheared-LLaMA-2.7B, Stupid Backoff trigram LMs (MUSE); base google/gemma-3-27b-it with google/gemma-3-4b-it small models for finance tasks. | “Throughout our experiments, we use the google/gemma-3-27b-it and google/gemma-3-4b-it models (Team, 2025).” |
| **baselines** | Target (no unlearning) and Retrain (retraining from scratch) on MUSE, plus prior unlearning methods GradDiff, NPO, SimNPO with OpenUnlearning defaults; un-adjusted Gemma 3 27B for airline portfolio task. | “For the other methods, we use the default settings provided by OpenUnlearning” |
| **headline_result** | MMLU CoT 0-shot utility largely preserved: Gemma-3-27b-it 77.94 vs 77.58 (linear, alpha=2) and 75.09 (TopK=250) after unlearning Split B; M&A memorization significantly reduced (figure only). | “\| google/gemma-3-27b-it \| 77.94” |
| **costs** | No trading costs; inference cost rises from 2N to 2(N+2n) FLOPs per token for small models of n parameters; trigram models add negligible overhead. | “Measured in FLOPs [18], the inference cost scales from” |
| **uncertainty** | 99% confidence intervals on finance tasks; standard errors computed by de-meaning groups and a population standard error; repeated prompting (4 times per deal filter, 30 runs for airline baseline). | “We calculated standard errors by de-meaning all groups and calculating a population standard error.” |
| **leakage_controls** | The method itself targets look-ahead bias: forget model fine-tuned on post-cutoff knowledge, retain model on pre-cutoff proxy; deals filtered to those memorized by 27B but not known by 4B. | “One small model is fine-tuned on the data to be forgotten, e.g., knowledge after 2010, while another is tuned on a proxy for the data to be retained, e.g., knowledge prior to 2010.” |
| **limitations** | Sensitivity to instruction tuning: if small models expect a different output structure, logit divergence may be diluted or noisy, producing unstable outputs; trigram models mainly useful for verbatim unlearning. | “A key limitation lies in the method’s sensitivity to instruction-tuning.” |
| **release** | Code and data said to be public on GitHub (link not given in text); also references frontiertopit.com. | “Everything was run on an H100 cluster unless otherwise noted. Code and data is available at GitHub.” |
